subject: URGENT: elevated 5xx/429s during customer traffic surge (FastShop)
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex@fastshop.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:15:21 -0700
Subject: High 5xx/429 during traffic spike — urgent

Sean —

We kicked off the staged launch at 08:45 PST and immediately saw a surge of 5xx and 429 responses. Our dashboard shows ~12% 5xx and 18% 429 over the first 20 minutes. Users are hitting timeouts and our client is aggressively retrying which looks like a retry storm.

Attached are server logs and a short trace from our SDK showing repeated retries. Can Redwood confirm whether throttling/policies changed on your side? We followed the ramp plan in the doc but the roll-forward went sideways.

Impact: checkout flows failing on mobile web, conversion drop is visible. This is high priority for our PM/eng team. Please advise immediate mitigations — we need a quick plan to stabilize traffic and reduce errors.

— Alex
CTO (Acting), FastShop
attachments: fastshop_prod_spike_logs_0504.zip, retry_trace_0504.txt

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@fastshop.com>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:26:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 during traffic spike — urgent

Alex — thanks for the alert and the artifacts. We're investigating now. Monica and Markus are on-call and will triage. Initial asks while we look:

- Can you pause aggressive client retries for the next 10 minutes (set backoff and jitter) and limit concurrency from the client to 50% of current?
- Share the exact ramp plan you started with (timestamps + target TPS). Link if it's on Drive.

Immediate actions from our side:
- Markus will validate if any rate-limiting or autoscaling events fired and whether the request router returned 429s due to token-bucket enforcement or internal queue saturation.
- If needed, we'll enable a temporary fallback route to a lower-capacity model variant to reduce per-token latency.
- I'm standing by to involve leadership if we need credits or capacity changes.

I'll update in 10 mins.

— Sean
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_quick_runbook.pdf

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex@fastshop.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:33:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 during traffic spike — urgent

Alex / team — I pulled metrics from the router and runtime. Quick summary:

- Root cause appears to be a client retry pattern coupled with a concentrated short-window ramp. Client retried with no jitter; many requests hit the same hot KV cache windows which amplified latency and caused internal request queue growth. Once the queue exceeded the soft-concurrency limit we started returning 429s and eventually some 5xx from downstream timeouts.
- Autoscale did not react fast enough due to the very short ramp (target TPS jumped ~8x in 3 minutes).

Immediate mitigations I applied (now):
- Enabled soft throttling at the request-router for the FastShop tenant to cap incoming TPS and favor requests with an exponential backoff header. This should reduce 5xx by preventing queue collapse.
- Activated a temporary fallback model (smaller quantized variant) for your endpoint — will reduce per-token latency but slightly change output distribution.

Please apply client-side backoff (150ms base, exponential, max 5s) and add jitter. If you can throttle your ramp to a 10–15 minute stair (2x every 2–3 minutes) we will keep the route unconstrained.

I'll keep monitoring and will share router logs in the next update.

— Markus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Rivera <alex@fastshop.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@fastshop.com
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:47:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx/429 during traffic spike — urgent

Thanks Markus — we pushed a runtime change to our SDK to add jitter/backoff and slowed the ramp to a 3-minute cadence. The 5xx rate dropped within ~6 minutes but we're still seeing intermittent timeouts (mostly 504s) and some user-facing errors.

Can Redwood confirm if enabling the fallback model is active for our production route and whether you can temporarily allocate dedicated capacity or a prioritized pool? Our product launch has contractual SLAs and we need short-term priority.

Also, please confirm the window for the temporary throttle — our engineers want to know how long to keep the ramp slowed.

— Alex

From: evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex@fastshop.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: FastShop launch impact — cc execs & next steps

Looping in leadership for temporary executive attention. Quick note for context: FastShop is in pipeline (deal FS-2026-88) and this launch impacts a high-visibility customer in North America.

Proposed short-term remedy (pending approval):
- Provide a 24-hour prioritized routing window on a dedicated burst pool (subject to capacity) to bring error rates under 1% while they finish ramping.
- Offer a goodwill credit for the incident window and a joint postmortem.
- Require the customer to adopt the stair-step ramp guidance and confirm SDK backoff applied.

Markus — please confirm capacity estimate for a 24-hour burst (GPU-hours and expected cost). Sean/Monica — please prepare comms; Alex — we need a sign-off on the slower ramp cadence and permission to route to a temporary prioritized pool.

— Evelyn
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex@fastshop.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 5 May 2026 16:30:12 -07:00
Subject: RESOLUTION & next steps — FastShop launch incident (postmortem pending)

Alex / team — closing the loop: after the client-side backoff + our router soft-throttle + fallback model activation, error rates dropped to <0.8% and 429s went below 1% for the remainder of the ramp. We stood up a prioritized burst pool for 12 hours (it consumed ~18 GPU-hours) which prevented further queue collapse while your team completed the staged ramp.

Immediate outcomes:
- Stabilized production within ~30 minutes of coordinated mitigations.
- Temporary prioritized pool used for 12 hours (billing credit applied against May usage).
- SDK guidance updated in our Launch Ramp doc (link above) to require exponential backoff + jitter and a minimum 10-minute stair ramp for any >3x TPS increases.

Next steps:
- Joint postmortem scheduled: Wed 2026-05-06 10:00 PDT (invite sent).
- Markus will create an ops playbook entry for retry storms + throttling and add a router metric alert threshold.
- Customer-facing comms and the credit confirmation will come from Monica.

Thanks to everyone who moved quickly — we'll follow up with the postmortem doc and action items.

— Sean
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
